The matrix \(B = A + tI\) is promised to have rank exactly 3. The hint further implies that this rank-3 matrix is traceless, so
\[
\operatorname{tr}(B) = \operatorname{tr}(A) + 192\, t \equiv 0 \pmod{p}.
\]
The trace of \(A\) is the sum of its 192 diagonal entries. Reducing that sum modulo \(p = 2147483647\) yields
\[
\operatorname{tr}(A) \equiv 827353889 \pmod{p}.
\]
Hence
\[
t \equiv -827353889 \cdot 192^{-1} \pmod{p}.
\]
The inverse of 192 is obtained from the factorisation \(192 = 2^6 \cdot 3\) together with the relations \(2^{31} \equiv 1 \pmod{p}\) and \(3 \cdot 1431655765 \equiv 1 \pmod{p}\):
\[
192^{-1} \equiv 727012693 \pmod{p}.
\]
The required modular product is
\[
827353889 \cdot 727012693 \equiv 1089235769 \pmod{p},
\]
and therefore
\[
t \equiv 2147483647 - 1089235769 = 1058247878 \pmod{p}.
\]
(The same congruence is recovered by reducing the 62-bit integer product via the identity \(2^{31} \equiv 1\).) This value of \(t\) is the unique field element making \(A + tI\) have rank 3.

<answer>2147483647, 1058247878</answer>
